current.text: In a mock auction, he went for 27 USD. The expert had expected a price in the mid 20s.

Experts price him about at market or a little below it. One sees him as a mid-third to early-fourth round pick in categories but is fine with his ADP of about 30. Another ranks him slightly below consensus and calls him a bit overvalued. A third is comfortable with him in tier five of the power forwards.
Last season he finished 41st in category leagues and 29th in points leagues.
Last season he had two calf strains. He came back early and played on a minutes restriction. He looked better in the playoffs.
Last season his usage was 22. He blocked a career-high number of shots and ranked fifth in the league in blocks. His rebounding was strong.
A bad free throw season (about 61%) is the main reason his fantasy value fell last season. He also shot under 30% from three after two straight seasons at 37%.
Experts expect his three-point shooting to recover toward 33 to 34%. One calls this a big year for him on offense.
He is projected to start at forward next to Jarrett Allen, with James Harden, Donovan Mitchell and Peyton Watson. There are no current injury concerns.
Cleveland's frontcourt depth is very thin. Behind Mobley and Allen there is only Thomas Bryant, then Ernest Udeh Jr. and Khalifa Diop. Dean Wade is gone.

Cleveland may close games with Mobley at center now that Peyton Watson is on the team. It is unclear whether Kenny Atkinson will use him more at center in small lineups or lean on Allen and Harden pick-and-rolls.
James Harden plays a full season in Cleveland, so more players need the ball. One expert is not sold on a big usage bump for Mobley.
Cleveland has the most back-to-backs in the league. With our March 28 end date, the Cavs play 4, 3 and then 2 games in the fantasy playoffs. The two-game week is finals week, starting March 22.
The weak playoff schedule gives one expert some pause on Mobley. Another calls the impact of the two-game week borderline for him.
Cleveland is projected to win about 51 to 53 games. Coach Kenny Atkinson is under pressure.

durable.text: He is an elite defender with a high floor and a good passer out of the pocket. The open question is whether his offense can take the next step.
Blocks are his best category and a real outlier against the league. Rebounds and FG% are also clear strengths.
Free throws are his clear weak spot. Experts expect his FT% to stay poor and say it will never be excellent. Any improvement would be a bonus.
He is 25 and not yet at his peak. He could become a 20-point scorer with two blocks per game.
He has a history of lower-body injuries, including two calf strains last season.

note: Mobley is a clear blocks, rebounds and FG% asset whose FT% is the only real hole, which makes him a natural punt FT% piece. The market has cooled on him. He went for 36 USD in our league last season, and Yahoo values him at 30 USD (average cost 27.1) and ESPN at 27 USD (average cost 21.4), so a price in the mid to high 20s, as in the recent mock, is fair; in a build that keeps FT% he is worth less. Early in the season, check whether his FT% climbs back toward 70% and his 3P% toward 33%, and how much he plays at center. Keep in mind the 2-game finals week and the league-high back-to-back count.
